title: Problem Identification & Gap Analysis
result: Gap analysis of VARAHA vs Normalizing Flow sampling in RIFT. Full report at outputs/code/task-002-gap-analysis.md.
key_findings: VARAHA uses uniform hypercube with threshold-driven volume pruning (no learned proposal)
NFlow uses MaskedAutoregressiveTransform trained on weighted samples (learned proposal)
Drop-in replacement NOT possible due to different draw signatures and weight correction terms
Both lack GPU sampling, checkpointing, and hybrid sampling modes
Minimum 10 valid samples required after weight filtering for NF training
Flow training triggered every chunk while n_adapt > 0, data = last n_history samples
integration_points_identified: Training data pipeline (sample accumulation, weight scaling, filtering)
Sampling loop modification (NF updates per chunk vs VARAHA implicit)
